newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Vilnius says pact with U.S. no substitute for NATO.
newsitem.headline: Vilnius says pact with U.S. no substitute for NATO.

text.p: The Baltic state of Lithuania said on Friday it was interested in negotiating a security charter with the United States but stressed such a pact could not be an alternative to NATO membership.

The Washington Post reported on Friday that the Clinton administration was offering to negotiate a security agreement with Lithuania and its Baltic neighbours Latvia and Estonia in an effort to ease their security conerns.
A U.S. diplomat confirmed to Reuters that such a proposal was under discussion in Washington.
"We would like to have these kinds of discussions with the U.S.," Lithuanian foreign affairs minister Algirdas Saudargas told Reuters.
"But this kind of security agreement would not be regarded as a substitute for NATO membership but as a path toward membership in the alliance."
Estonian and Latvian officials were not immediately available to comment because of the Easter holidays. Good Friday is a working day in Lithuania.
The three small Baltic countries, anxious to secure their hard-fought independence, view NATO's protective embrace as their only shield from a potentially hostile Russia.
But diplomats say the three are not likely to be invited into the alliance because of Moscow's strong objections.
NATO is expected to invite Poland, Hungary, the Czech republic and possibly Slovenia for accession talks during a summit in Madrid in July.
Saudargas reiterated Lithunia's position that at least one Baltic state should be allowed into the alliance.
"Our position is that at least one Baltic country be invited to join the alliance," he said.
